claim_lines.text: Backward pruning removes a state only if it has no allowed successor; forward pruning removes it only if no allowed predecessor remains. Neither operation can remove a member of an actual compatible path. An actual static map uses the same mask whenever B repeats. Intersecting supported masks across all occurrences of B cannot remove that map's mask. Induction over monotone sweeps proves that every compatible physical anchor remains in the returned root support. Eight sweeps need not reach a fixed point: stopping early preserves a weaker necessary superset, never a stronger rejection. A time/memory interruption instead leaves the whole controller unresolved; no partial support is returned as a proved zero.
